acceptance.generations: Opt-in immutable retired generations for replacement and deletion; opaque owner/key-bound history IDs, private capabilities and verified bytes.
acceptance.fencing: Current signed reads bind provider generations; stale signed/public reads recheck generation after I/O. Restore snapshots the destination generation before reads and fences it through reservation/commit, including identical-digest replacements.
acceptance.retries: Current object and restore receipt commit together. Exact owner-bound retries survive restart and source byte eviction until the original age deadline, without another provider write. Changed input conflicts; expired source IDs cannot execute again.
acceptance.retention: Independent age, per-object count, total generation count, bucket bytes and owner bytes; strict bounds, newest-first priority, tightened policies, startup retirement and durable provider cleanup. At most 1000 generations per bucket and 10000 live receipts per manager.
acceptance.authority: User owner/key isolation; authenticated history even for public app buckets. CSRF-gated restore, current-session refresh after body parsing and inside commit; revocation through an independent backend connection rolls back body/provider races. Standalone adapters must supply synchronous current checks; direct server/MCP adapters remain trusted authorization boundaries.
acceptance.failure: Quota, receipt capacity, provider, expiry, corruption, deletion/recreation and callback failures preserve current bytes and release reservations. Snapshot/receipt ownership mismatch fails integrity checks.
acceptance.browser: Built-in History links, private downloads, nonce-protected restore forms, visible status and retained keyboard focus. Actual browser/Node HTTP/SQLite auth/local-store flow verifies keyboard restore, exact retained download bytes, stale-file rejection, 390px contained overflow and revoked restore access.

before.scope: Isolated old-current-read regression on the pre-feature build; a signed URL silently returns replacement bytes.

compatibility.default: Retention disabled; existing current quotas remain separate from retained capacity. New generation binding intentionally invalidates legacy unbound current-read tokens.
compatibility.migration: Additive clank_bucket_versions and clank_bucket_restore_receipts tables; immutable provider keys reused without copying retired bytes.
compatibility.rollback: Disable versions using upgraded manager and sweep; stop before old binary, disable history/restore, rotate signing key. Old code cannot enforce generation-bound reads, and code reversion alone does not reclaim retained bytes.
compatibility.dependencies: No npm dependencies; same 395-file and 6 MiB package gates.

boundaries.bearerCapabilities: History capabilities remain valid independently of human session until their bounded expiry/retention deadline; revoked sessions cannot mint new capabilities or restore.
boundaries.appOwnership: Application-owned history is shared; use server-only buckets and protected server actions for additional role checks.
boundaries.receipts: Historical accepted metadata can describe a generation that later uploads replaced.
boundaries.cleanup: Inaccessible garbage consumes physical bytes until provider deletion succeeds.
boundaries.host: Privileged Docker/XFS certification still requires an explicitly disposable compatible host; three privileged-host skips are not certification.

delivery.merge: protected squash with expected head; no bypass
